properties.decision: ACCEPTED on Anthony's word, 2026-08-08 — shape (a), and he named why it is the right one: it is the only option where the question STOPS EXISTING rather than being answered. No plan ever holds a number it can lose, so neither slipping nor inserting is a problem. THE RULE: a planned increment's identity names its CONTENT (`epoch:planned-read-half`, `epoch:planned-status-accounting`). The version number is not part of the plan at all. At cut time the number is derived from what actually shipped, by the CHANGELOG's own bucket table — patch for fixes, minor for a change to the shape of the tool surface or the schema. WHAT IT DISSOLVES: (1) The id churn. An id cannot be renamed, so a version-named plan guarantees either a lying id or a node replacement that breaks the snapshot trail `dec:arrival-delta` reads plan movement from. A content-named plan never needs renaming, because content is what the plan IS. (2) The slip-versus-insert question entirely. `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` (accepted an hour earlier) and `dec:idea-an-unplanned-cut-takes-an-in-between-number` were competing answers to "what happens to the planned numbers when unplanned work takes one" — and under this rule there are no planned numbers to disturb. The slip rule is not WRONG; its subject ceases to exist. Recorded with an OBSOLETES edge rather than by un-accepting it, per dec:reopen-supersedes: an accepted Decision is never un-accepted. (3) The pressure to mislabel. With numbering decided at the cut from shipped content, semver stays honest by construction — nobody is tempted to call a shape change a patch to protect a planned number, which is the concrete harm the in-between-number idea carried (the CHANGELOG's own table says patch means the consumer updates blindly). THE OBSERVATION UNDERNEATH, which generalises past versioning: a version number is assigned LAST, at the cut, and a planned increment exists LONG before that. Baking it into the identity records a GUESS as a NAME. That is the same shape as `ver:plan-increments`' finding that a plan's content lived in an epoch's NAME as prose rather than as structure — both are a plan carrying, in its identity or its label, something that belongs elsewhere. COMPOSES WITH THE HYBRID rather than competing: content-named plans plus semver-honest numbering at cut time is the same destination reached from two directions, which is why `dec:idea-an-unplanned-cut-takes-an-in-between-number` stays recorded rather than rejected — its numbering instinct survives, only its premise (that plans own numbers) is gone. NOT CHOSEN: (b) a `version` property on DesignEpoch — smaller, but it leaves the misleading ids in place; (c) redefining the pre-1.0 buckets — cheapest to write, most expensive to be wrong about, since it weakens the one signal consumers act on blindly; (d) keeping version-named ids and reading them as birth numbers — makes every id a small trap for a future reader.
properties.name: A planned increment is identified by what it DELIVERS; the version number is assigned at the cut, from what actually shipped
properties.rationale: Raised immediately after applying the slip, because the cost was concrete rather than theoretical: four planned epochs needed renaming and none could have its id corrected, so the graph now holds ids whose numbers are one behind their content. Recorded rather than fixed — changing how the plan is ADDRESSED is a bigger act than the slip Anthony asked for, and picking (a) would re-point every future reference.
